correctness.rationale: For any interior initial condition and \(0<\alpha<1\) the exact scalar identity \(2z_{j+1}-1=(2z_j-1)^2\) and the doubly stochastic cycle projection prove the equilibrium coordinate formula. Under Dirichlet input, independent exponential marks give the exact \(M_n=(n/S_n)U_n\) relation. Conditional gamma probabilities and the permutation cycle index yield an exact finite-n generating function. Chernoff bounds make its analytic factor regular past \(z=1\) and imply exponential convergence of U_n CDF for each \(t>1\). Lagrange inversion for Poisson Galton--Watson total finite progeny and matching derivatives, with constants at infinity, prove the closed CDF. Continuity at t=1 and Slutsky finish. The critical/tail expansions follow from the fixed-point equation. Standalone finite checks were executed; they are corroboration, not substitutes for proof.

evidence: The cycle-average projection follows from Jamilov, but its full random-distribution CDF additionally requires independent Dirichlet sampling, uniform cycle-index enumeration, gamma-tail control for all lengths, and the Lagrange branching identity.
Mathieu--Wilson (arXiv:1201.3955) study minimum mean-weight cycles in a complete random network, not maximum means on disjoint cycles of one uniform permutation.
Galganov--Ilienko provide short-cycle Poisson limits that could be used as an alternate probabilistic route to the unnormalized limit, but do not state the branching identity.

Potential broader hidden coverage remains possible.

originality.rationale: The full 2022 permutation-QSO text proves fixed-parameter convergence and invariant cycle masses, not the random-permutation/uniform-initial-condition maximum-equilibrium law. The full 2023 permutation-cycle paper establishes point-process laws and short-cycle statistics without an independent exponential cycle-average maximum or branching-extinction CDF. Classical cycle-index and Borel total-progeny expansions are treated as existing methods. The new conjunction is a distributional theorem for a specified high-dimensional dynamical population ensemble with a sharply identified CDF. Relevant 2024 related full text was unavailable, and unindexed equivalent probability results remain a substantive priority risk.
residual_risks: The full text of the 2023/2024 same-object Jamilov--Khudoyberdiev article was not accessible; its abstract was inspected and no claim of whole-document NOT_COVERING is made.
An earlier unindexed probability theorem could identify the maximum of independent exponential cycle means with branching survival via a general maximum-cycle-mean or forest identity.
A short-cycle Poisson-point theorem may imply the unnormalized limit abstractly, though the closed branching-law identification and application were not found stated.

value.rationale: A natural observable in a published population-genetics dynamical family is the largest surviving equilibrium coordinate. For a high-dimensional randomly permuted interaction structure and a uniform initial composition, the theorem gives its exact nondegenerate scaling, sharp support threshold, full limiting CDF, near-critical slope, tail, and independence from fixed interior mixing strength. This is not a restatement of deterministic convergence or a known fixed-cycle calculation; it reveals an unexpected explicit branching-survival law across two mathematical settings. No more general biological or statistical universality is claimed.
